themes.label: Profanity / taboo language used for emphasis or insults
themes.interpretation: Posts use explicit expletives and taboo insults; this appears more strongly in the remove-rated group, suggesting profanity/insulting register is a key moderation risk signal here.

themes.label: Political blame via us-vs-them / targeted attribution
themes.interpretation: Content attributes blame to specific political actors or groups (e.g., US/Trump) or directs hostility toward a profession/group (e.g., journalists), aligning with hostile targeting patterns.

themes.label: Conspiratorial or hidden-coordination claims
themes.interpretation: Some remove-rated content asserts coordinated influence by concealed organizations (e.g., dark money/think tanks), indicating conspiracy framing as a moderation-relevant theme.

themes.label: Election/voter process claims (voter ID, registration, participation mechanics)
themes.interpretation: A remove-rated post centers on election/voting mechanics (voter ID and registration) and frames them as illegal or suppression-related—moderation may flag procedural-election claims when combined with other risk factors.

themes.label: Causal/evidence-oriented economic or policy linkage
themes.interpretation: Keep-rated content frames cost-of-living/benefits topics and uses causal/evidence-style language (e.g., outcomes tied to interest costs) rather than hostile or conspiratorial rhetoric.

themes.label: Accountability / oversight as a normative requirement
themes.interpretation: Keep-rated messaging explicitly invokes scrutiny/oversight and accountability norms, which contrasts with the more aggressive or contemptuous framing in remove-rated examples.

themes.label: Conditional policy “if-then” downstream effects
themes.interpretation: Keep-rated content uses conditional structures to predict downstream outcomes from policy passage, suggesting more explanatory/analytical rhetoric.

themes.label: Event-claiming with quoted/foreknowledge framing
themes.interpretation: Remove-rated content presents a specific quoted warning/foreknowledge as factual (e.g., “said months before”), indicating risk where strong event-witnessing claims are asserted.

cross_cutting_themes: Use of political framing (blame attribution, election process discussion) spans multiple themes and appears in both keep and remove groups.
Hostile rhetoric escalation (profanity/insults/ridicule) strongly clusters in remove-rated examples and intersects with targeted directionality.
Risky belief-structure claims (conspiracy framing, strong event-assertion/foreknowledge) appear in remove-rated themes alongside conspiratorial or factual-extrapolation cues.
